steps.body: Grids of squares show up everywhere — a chocolate bar, a window with panes, a checkerboard. Counting the grid tells you exactly how many pieces there are.

widget.prompt: A rectangle is partitioned into 4 rows and 6 columns of unit squares. How many unit squares in all?

commonCounts.feedback: That's 4 + 6. Count every square in the grid: 24.
That's just one row. Count all 4 rows: 24 in all.

widget.successFeedback: 4 rows of 6 squares each makes 24 squares in all.

steps.body: The same grid-counting idea applies to any real object split into rows and columns.
takeaways: Chocolate bars, windows, checkerboards, tiles — all grids of squares.
Count every square in every row, no matter the object.
The counting rule never changes, only the size of the grid.
